visual_text: Noisy breathing near death: what you may hear
Saliva and mucus collect in the throat when a person can no longer clear them
Changing the person's position is one usual way to manage the sound
Ask the nurse to explain what you are hearing
Studies generally find the sound does not distress the person; few looked at patients
Wee and Hillier, Cochrane 2008; Fagan et al., 2025
Alasdair MacLullich | Small detail, real effect
alt_text: Bedside scene: an older man lies in a hospital bed, a woman sits beside him and a nurse stands at the bedside. Three numbered markers explain noisy breathing near death: saliva collects in the throat, changing position is one usual way to manage the sound, and ask the nurse to explain. Studies generally find it does not distress the person; few looked at patients.
